question: Who among the following social reformers of British India was known as Lokhitwadi?
solution:
The correct answer is** Gopal Hari Deshmukh.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Gopal Hari Deshmukh (1823-1892) was a social reformer and rationalist from Maharashtra.
 
• He held the post of a judge under the British raj but wrote for a weekly Prabhakar under the pen name of Lokahitawadi on social reform issues.
 
• He wrote 'Shatpatre' in the Prabhakar newspaper. In 'Shatapatre' he wrote about Political, Religious, Social, Cultural topics.
 
• He was against Child Marriage, the Dowry system, Polygamy.
 
• He also criticized the Caste System in society.
 
• He was a supporter of Girls Education.
 
• He advocated a reorganization of Indian society on rational principles and modern, humanistic, secular values.
 
• He attacked Hindu orthodoxy and supported social and religious equality.
 
• **After bearing public criticism he served lame, blind and leprosy persons. **
 
• He wrote against the evils of the caste system. He said, “If religion does not sanction social reform, then change religion”.
 
• He started a weekly, "Hitechhu", and also played a leading role in founding the periodicals, Gyan Prakash, Indu Prakash, and Lokahitawadi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jyotiba Phule****​**

 
 
• Jyotirao Phule was a social reformer, activist, and writer who lived in the 19th century in Maharashtra, India.
 
• He founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 with the aim of uplifting the lower castes and women through education and social reforms.
 
• The Satyashodhak Samaj was a movement that challenged the caste system and advocated for social equality and justice.
 
• Jyotirao Phule was also a strong advocate of women's education and established the first school for girls in Pune in 1848.
 
 
 
• **Veeresalingam Pantu**lu ​
 
 
• Veeresalingam Pantulu (16 April 1848 – 27 May 1919) was a famous social reformer and writer of the modern period of Telugu literature.
 
• He was known by the title 'Gadya Tikkana' and was often considered 'Raja Ram Mohan Roy' of Andhra.
 
• Born in a Brahmin family, Veeresalingam Pantalu was a staunch opponent of the caste system and started the anti-caste movement.
 
• He established widow ashrams and formed an association for Widow Remarriage in Madras Presidency.
 
• To encourage women's education, he established schools for girls in 1874 at Dowlaiswaram near Rajahmundry.
 
• Veeresalingam Pantulu earned a reputation as the first novelist, the first playwright, and the originator of modern journalism.
